result.headline: The whole-board MLP scores 31.5 apples on average over 3 seeds (test), while the CNN scores 12.4 in the same 10 minutes: it runs about 6x fewer steps and is also behind per step.
result.summary:
**MLP (full vision, DQN):** the three seeds scored 30.97, 31.87 and 31.64 test apples (mean 31.49, std 0.47). Over 605k env steps in 10 minutes (about 1,000 steps/s), the training mean of the last 100 games rose from 2.1 at 0.9 min to 18.6 at 1.8 min and then flattened at 20.6 to 23.2 for the last six minutes. Only 0 of 100 test games ended by starving, and 65 of 100 ended by the snake running into its own body. A 'dqn' test game lasted about 269 steps and took 9 steps per apple.

**CNN (same vision, three 3x3 conv layers):** the test scores were 11.76, 12.08 and 13.25 (mean 12.4). It ran only about 94k env steps in 10 minutes (about 157 steps/s), and its training mean was 6.4 to 10.4. Of its 100 test games, 99 ended in a body crash, after about 86 steps and 7 steps per apple. It eats efficiently but walks into its own tail early. The gap between the two networks (about 19 points) is far larger than the seed spread (under 1.5 points in each group), so it is not noise. Note that the throughput numbers are from a shared machine: lesson 02 ran the same MLP recipe and got only about 90k steps, so compare step counts only within this lesson.
result.diagnosis:
The CNN's deficit has two parts. First, speed: the convolutions make each step about 6x more expensive, so in a fixed 10 minutes it sees far fewer games and updates. Second, per-step learning: at roughly 94k to 118k steps the MLP already had a training mean of 18.6, while the CNN was at 6.4 to 10.4. So the CNN is not simply catching up per step either. Its learning rate (0.001), target sync (500) and exploration schedule were copied from the MLP recipe and never tuned for convolutions, so that part may be a tuning problem, not a fact about CNNs.

The MLP's flat curve after about 4 minutes, together with its 65 to 72 percent body-crash share, suggests that more of the same training will not help much. The snake eats efficiently (9 steps per apple) but traps itself in its own body. The death penalty is one lever for that, and the reward catalog lets you split it into a wall and a body penalty.
result.learned: Seeing more of the board does not help if the network needs far more compute per step: under equal wall-clock time the CNN lost badly, and its per-step learning was also worse here. Compare methods by score per env step and by steps per second separately, and treat one seed as a single sample.
result.prediction_check: Partly. The prediction that the CNN gets fewer steps in 10 minutes held (about 94k vs 605k, about 6x fewer). It did not hold that the CNN would still learn the pattern well enough to stay competitive: it scored 12.4 against the MLP's 31.5.

recommendations.title: Give the CNN 60 minutes
recommendations.why: If the CNN is only slow, then a 60-minute run gives it roughly the 600k steps the MLP had in 10 minutes. If it still trails, the gap is per-step learning, not just speed.
recommendations.change: Keep the CNN network and extend the training time from 10 to 60 minutes.
recommendations.prediction: The CNN's test mean rises to about 25 to 33 apples (the MLP's 10-minute score is 31.5), and its body-crash share stays above 80 percent.
recommendations.question: Is the CNN's deficit just speed, or does it also learn less from each step?

recommendations.title: Penalise body crashes harder
recommendations.why: The MLP dies in its own body in 65 to 72 percent of test games. Splitting the death penalty and raising the body penalty tests whether the snake avoids self-trapping when that mistake costs more.
recommendations.change: Replace the single death penalty with separate wall (10) and body (30) penalties.
recommendations.prediction: Body crashes fall below 60 percent of test games. The test mean moves by less than 3 points, since lesson 05 showed a higher penalty can cut body crashes without raising the score.
recommendations.question: Does weighting the body crash more heavily reduce self-trapping and raise the score?
warnings: Crashing costs more than an apple is worth, but starving costs less and time is free: the snake may learn to loop until it starves rather than risk a crash. Raise the starvation penalty or add a hunger cost.

ideas.title: Step-matched comparison view on the dashboard
ideas.what: Add a chart that plots training and test scores against environment steps for every run in a lesson, next to the existing wall-clock chart, so learners can compare methods at equal steps.
ideas.why: The CNN and MLP ranking is clear on the wall-clock chart, but it hides whether the CNN is worse per step. Equal-step comparisons would separate the speed effect from the learning effect, which this run's question depends on.
ideas.expected: Learners can see at a glance whether the CNN is behind at equal steps (here, about 6 vs 18 at roughly 100k steps) or only in wall-clock time.

ideas.title: Learning-rate decay during training
ideas.what: Add an option that lowers the learning rate on a schedule, for example halving it every fixed number of steps, applied to DQN.
ideas.why: The MLP's training mean stalled at 20.6 to 23.2 from about 3.6 minutes to the end, after exploration had mostly finished (at 100k steps), so a lower learning rate later may help it settle.
ideas.expected: A few points on the MLP's plateau (for example from about 31 toward 33 to 35 test apples), though this is a guess that needs testing over several seeds.
